docs.text: HardFOC driver TLE92466ED Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the Infineon TLE92466ED six-channel low-side solenoid driver. It brings the chip up, configures current control, PWM and dither per channel, regulates solenoid and valve currents and reads back feedback and diagnostics, on any MCU with an SPI bus. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that moves 32-bit SPI frames and sets three pins; it does the rest: frame encoding with the CRC byte, the one-frame reply pipeline, reply validation, current scaling and fault decoding. API guide ¶ How to do the common jobs with the driver: bring the chip up, configure channels, drive currents, read feedback and handle errors. Every snippet on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp , with Driver standing for tle92466ed::Driver<MySpi> . The API reference lists every member. The shape of the API ¶ One Driver<Comm> object per chip. Its members fall into these groups: Group Members Mode Bring-up and modes Init() , EnterMissionMode() , EnterMissionModeChecked() , EnterConfigMode() , IsMissionMode() Global configuration ConfigureGlobal() , SetCrcEnabled() , SetVbatThresholds() , SetVioLevel() , ConfigureClockSource() Config Channel setup SetChannelMode() , ConfigureChannel() , SetParallelOperation() Config Current, PWM, dither SetCurrentSetpoint() , SetCurrentSetpointUa() , ConfigurePwmPeriod() , ConfigureDither() , ConfigureDitherClock() Any Switching EnableChannel() , EnableChannels() , EnableAllChannels() , DisableAllChannels() Mission Feedback GetAverageCurrent() , GetDutyCycle() , ReadChannelFeedback() , SampleChannelCurrents() , ReadAllSupplyVoltages() Any Faults GetAllFaults() , GetDeviceStatus() , GetChannelDiagnostics() , ClearFaults() , IsFault() , SetFaultMask() Any Watchdog and identity ReloadSpiWatchdog() , VerifyDevice() , GetIcVersion() , GetChipId() Any Control pins HoldReset() , ReleaseReset() , Enable() , Disable() Any Registers ReadRegister() , ReadRegisterMulti() , WriteRegister() , ModifyRegister() Any Channels are tle92466ed::Channel::CH0 to CH5 . Every call returns a DriverResult<T> and never throws: test it with if (!r) and read r.error() , a DriverError . Initialise ¶ bool bring_up ( Driver & driver ) { auto r = driver . Init (); // RESN pulse, EN high, ICVID check, defaults; ends in Config Mode if ( ! r ) { if ( r . error () == DriverError :: WrongDeviceID ) { std :: printf ( "not a TLE92466ED (ICVID high byte is not 0xC1) 
 " ); } else if ( r . error () == DriverError :: FaultDetected ) { std :: printf ( "critical fault frame: check VDD (5 V) and VIO first 
 " ); } return false ; } return true ; } Init() initialises your port, pulses RESN (10 ms low, 50 ms settle), sets EN, reads ICVID up to five times, refuses unprogrammed silicon, writes defaults (every channel ICC , setpoint 0, clock watchdog on, CRC and SPI watchdog off) and clears the power-on flags. Init(false) skips the RESN pulse, for a retry on a shared bus. Configure ¶ Configure in Config Mode, before EnterMissionMode() : the chip accepts channel modes, the global configuration and parallel pairs only there. // In Config Mode: mode, PWM period and dither for one channel. bool configure_channel ( Driver & driver , Channel ch ) { return driver . SetChannelMode ( ch , tle92466ed :: ChannelMode :: ICC ) && driver . ConfigurePwmPeriod ( ch , 500.0F ) && // 500 us = 2 kHz driver . ConfigureDither ( ch , 40.0F , 200.0F ); // 40 mA at 200 Hz; also starts Tmeas } ConfigureChannel() sets everything about a channel in one call (mode, setpoint, slew rate, diagnosis current, open-load threshold, PWM, dither); Configuration lists the fields of ChannelConfig and GlobalConfig . Current control gives the ranges and formulas behind the PWM and dither calls. Drive a current ¶ bool drive ( Driver & driver , Channel ch , uint16_t milliamps ) { if ( ! driver . IsMissionMode () && ! driver . EnterMissionMode ()) { return false ; } return driver . SetCurrentSetpoint ( ch , milliamps ) && // specified up to 1500 mA driver . EnableChannel ( ch , true ); } bool stop_all ( Driver & driver ) { return driver . DisableAllChannels (). has_value (); } SetCurrentSetpoint() takes milliamperes ( SetCurrentSetpointUa() microamperes) and can be called in either mode; the current flows once the channel is enabled in Mission Mode with EN high. Pass parallel_mode = true for the master channel of a parallel pair. Read feedback ¶ void report ( Driver & driver , Channel ch ) { if ( auto i = driver . GetAverageCurrent ( ch ); i ) { std :: printf ( "I_avg = %u mA 
 " , * i ); } else if ( i . error () == DriverError :: FeedbackNotReady ) { std :: printf ( "no measurement window yet (dither clock not running?) 
 " ); } if ( auto dc = driver . GetDutyCycle ( ch ); dc ) { std :: printf ( "duty = %u.%02u %% 
 " , * dc / 100U , * dc % 100U ); } if ( auto v = driver . ReadAllSupplyVoltages (); v ) { std :: printf ( "VBAT %u mV, VIO %u mV, VDD %u mV 
 " , v -> vbat_mV , v -> vio_mV , v -> vdd_mV ); } } GetAverageCurrent() waits for a completed measurement window (up to about 8 ms) and is meant for consoles and diagnostics. Supplies come back in millivolts. In a control loop, sample instead: // Control loop: one pipelined burst for several channels, never blocks. void control_tick ( Driver & driver ) { constexpr uint8_t kChannels = 0b000111 ; // CH0..CH2 auto batch = driver . SampleChannelCurrents ( kChannels ); if ( ! batch ) { return ; } for ( unsigned n = 0 ; n < 6 ; ++ n ) { if (( batch -> valid_mask & ( 1U << n )) != 0U ) { const int32_t ma = batch -> channels [ n ]. iavg_ma ; // use it in your current loop ( void ) ma ; } } // batch->rejected_chains > 0 means replies arrived out of order on the bus. } SampleChannelCurrents() reads every requested channel in one pipelined burst and never waits: a channel whose window is not ready keeps its bit clear in valid_mask and is picked up on the next tick. Use any register directly ¶ bool raw_access ( Driver & driver ) { namespace reg = tle92466ed :: CentralReg ; auto id = driver . ReadRegister ( reg :: ICVID ); // 0xC1xx: type 0xC1, silicon revision in the low byte if ( ! id ) { return false ; } const uint16_t setpoint = tle92466ed :: GetChannelRegister ( Channel :: CH1 , tle92466ed :: ChannelReg :: SETPOINT ); return driver . ModifyRegister ( setpoint , 0x7FFF , 0x1000 ). has_value (); // TARGET bits only } Central registers are in tle92466ed::CentralReg ; channel registers are an offset in ChannelReg added to the channel's base ( GetChannelRegister() ). WriteRegister() reads the value back by default; ModifyRegister() reads, masks and writes. Writes reach only 0x00 to 0x7F ( SPI protocol ). Errors ¶ DriverError Meaning First thing to check NotInitialized Init() has not succeeded Call order WrongMode Needs Config Mode (configuration) or Mission Mode (enable) EnterConfigMode() / EnterMissionMode() InvalidChannel , InvalidParameter Argument out of range Channel, setpoint scale, PWM period DeviceNotResponding MISO idle on every attempt Power, VIO, CSN, MISO wiring CRCError Replies arrived but none passed CRC and width checks SPI mode, clock speed, CSN timing, shared bus SPIFrameError The chip flagged the previous frame (status field) Frame length (exactly 32 bits), CRC FaultDetected Critical-fault reply VDD, internal supplies, clock ( SPI protocol ) WrongDeviceID ICVID is not 0xC1xx Another device on CSN, wrong SPI mode RegisterError A write did not read back Bus integrity, Mission Mode restrictions FeedbackNotReady No measurement window yet Dither clock ( ConfigureDither() ), feedback frozen ConfigurationError Unprogrammed OTP, or a configuration the chip rejected The part, the arguments TimeoutError A wait (feedback, mission mode, BIST) ran out Timeout argument, chip state HardwareError Your port returned an error The port Faults the chip detects are not errors of the call; read them with GetAllFaults() : void handle_faults ( Driver & driver ) { auto pin = driver . IsFault (); // FAULTN low? if ( ! pin || !* pin ) { return ; } auto report = driver . GetAllFaults (); if ( ! report ) { return ; } if ( report -> vbat_uv || report -> vdd_uv ) { std :: printf ( "supply under-voltage 
 " ); } for ( unsigned n = 0 ; n < report -> channels . size (); ++ n ) { const auto & c = report -> channels [ n ]; if ( c . open_load || c . short_to_ground || c . overcurrent || c . over_temperature ) { std :: printf ( "CH%u: OL=%d SG=%d OC=%d OT=%d 
 " , n , c . open_load , c . short_to_ground , c . overcurrent , c . over_temperature ); } } ( void ) driver . ClearFaults (); // after the cause is fixed; a fault that is still there comes back } Diagnostics and faults explains every fault source; Troubleshooting maps symptoms to causes. Keep the SPI watchdog fed ¶ // With GlobalConfig::spi_watchdog_enabled, call this faster than the watchdog runs out. bool kick_watchdog ( Driver & driver ) { return driver . ReloadSpiWatchdog ( 1000 ). has_value (); } Only needed when you enable the watchdog in ConfigureGlobal() ; the timeout table converts WD_TIME to milliseconds. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each chip one owner task, or guard every call on a driver object (and its port) with one mutex.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is put together: three layers, what each owns, and how one call reaches the chip. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one Driver object per chip. The core owns the chip's register map (from inc/tle92466ed_registers.hpp): the central configuration and status registers, and the bank of channel registers that repeats for each of the six channels. The communication interface (tle92466ed::SpiInterface in inc/tle92466ed_spi_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base: it builds 32-bit frames with the CRC-8 SAE J1850 byte, runs the one-frame reply pipeline and validates every reply; the methods it dispatches to your class are listed from the header. The platform port is the only code you write. Below it is the chip. Drawn from: inc/tle92466ed_registers.hpp CentralReg ; inc/tle92466ed_registers.hpp ChannelReg ; inc/tle92466ed_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . The three layers ¶ Layer Where Depends on You change it when Hardware-agnostic core : Driver<Comm> tle92466ed.hpp The interface Never, for a new board Communication interface : SpiInterface<Self> tle92466ed_spi_interface.hpp Your port's methods Never Platform port : your class Your project Your SDK Once per MCU or board ( Porting ) Everything above the port is the same on ESP32, STM32, a Linux host or the unit-test model. That is how the host tests run the real driver code without hardware. What each layer owns ¶ The core knows the chip: the register map and bit fields, Config and Mission Mode, the channel bank addresses, setpoint and PWM scaling, the feedback decoding and the fault report. It caches what the chip does not read back reliably (the channel-enable bits of CH_CTRL ) and checks the mode before calls that need one. The interface knows the bus protocol: it builds the 32-bit frames, adds the CRC byte, sends the flush / command / dummy sequence, checks each reply's CRC and width, and records critical-fault frames. It also offers ReadMulti() , a pipelined burst of up to 12 reads. The port knows your hardware: how to clock 32 bits with CSN, how to set two GPIOs and read one, how to wait and where log lines go. How one call reaches the chip ¶ sequenceDiagram participant A as Application participant D as Driver core participant I as SpiInterface participant P as Your port A->>D: SetCurrentSetpoint(CH0, 500) D->>D: TARGET = 500 x 32767 / 2000 = 8192 D->>I: Write(CH0 SETPOINT, 8192) I->>P: TransferMulti(flush, write frame, dummy) P-->>I: three reply words I-->>D: status and CRC of the write reply D->>I: Read(CH0 SETPOINT) I->>P: TransferMulti(flush, read frame, dummy) P-->>I: three reply words I-->>D: TARGET read back D-->>A: success, or an error SetCurrentSetpoint() reads the setpoint back and retries a write that did not land, up to three times. Why CRTP ¶ The interface is a class template parameter, not a virtual base class. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them; the driver has no vtable, allocates nothing and needs no RTTI. The cost is that the driver type names the port: Driver<MySpi> . Code that has to work with several port types takes the driver as a template parameter too. Errors without exceptions ¶ Every call returns DriverResult<T> , an expected<T, DriverError> : std::expected on C++23, a small polyfill on C++20. The interface returns CommResult<T> with a CommError , which the core maps to a DriverError ( NoReply to DeviceNotResponding , a critical-fault frame to FaultDetected , and so on). The API guide lists them. It caches what the chip does not read back reliably (the channel-enable bits of CH_CTRL ) and checks the mode before calls that need one. The interface knows the bus protocol: it builds the 32-bit frames, adds the CRC byte, sends the flush / command / dummy sequence, checks each reply's CRC and width, and records critical-fault frames. It also offers ReadMulti() , a pipelined burst of up to 12 reads. The port knows your hardware: how to clock 32 bits with CSN, how to set two GPIOs and read one, how to wait and where log lines go.

docs.text: The interface is a class template parameter, not a virtual base class. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them; the driver has no vtable, allocates nothing and needs no RTTI. The cost is that the driver type names the port: Driver<MySpi> . Code that has to work with several port types takes the driver as a template parameter too.

docs.text: Every call returns DriverResult<T> , an expected<T, DriverError> : std::expected on C++23, a small polyfill on C++20. The interface returns CommResult<T> with a CommError , which the core maps to a DriverError ( NoReply to DeviceNotResponding , a critical-fault frame to FaultDetected , and so on). The API guide lists them.

docs.text: Current control ¶ How the TLE92466ED regulates a coil current, how the driver scales setpoints, PWM and dither, and when current feedback is valid. Section references are to the datasheet (Rev. 1.2). f SYS is 28 MHz. Channel modes ¶ A channel's mode is set in Config Mode ( SetChannelMode() or ChannelConfig::mode ) and decides how the output switches and which period the feedback averages over. ChannelMode Output Feedback period T meas OFF Off No measurement ICC Integrated current control to the SETPOINT target Dither period T Dither DIRECT_DRIVE_SPI On-time from the TON register T Dither DIRECT_DRIVE_DRV0 , DIRECT_DRIVE_DRV1 Follows the DRV0 / DRV1 pin T Dither if configured, else the DRV period FREE_RUN_MEAS Switch off; the shunt measures only T Dither Init() sets every channel to ICC with a zero setpoint. Setpoint ¶ The 15-bit TARGET field of each channel's SETPOINT register sets the average current: Mode Formula Full scale One LSB Specified range Single channel I set = 2 A × TARGET / (2 15 − 1) 2 A 61 µA 0 mA to 1500 mA Parallel pair I set = 4 A × TARGET / (2 15 − 1) 4 A 122 µA up to 2.7 A SetCurrentSetpoint(channel, mA, parallel) and SetCurrentSetpointUa(channel, µA, parallel) round to the nearest TARGET . They accept the full register scale (2000 mA, 4000 mA in parallel) and refuse anything above it with InvalidParameter ; keep the steady-state setpoint inside the specified range. After the write the driver reads SETPOINT back and retries up to three times. GetCurrentSetpoint() converts the register back to mA. The controller is an integrator: it switches the output on and off so that the average current over a PWM period matches the target. Accuracy is ±2.5 mA from 10 mA to 250 mA and ±1 % above (single channel, section 4.6.3). PWM period ¶ The PWM frequency controller adjusts the switching period to a target set in the PERIOD register (section 4.6.2.3): Range Formula Period Frequency Standard ( LOW_FREQ_RANGE_EN = 0) T = PERIOD_MANT × 2 PERIOD_EXP / f SYS 250 µs to 9.09 ms 4 kHz to 110 Hz Low frequency ( LOW_FREQ_RANGE_EN = 1) T = PERIOD_MANT × 8 × 2 PERIOD_EXP / f SYS 2 ms to 72.7 ms 500 Hz to 13.75 Hz The datasheet specifies the controller for 110 Hz to 4 kHz; the low-frequency limits are that range divided by eight. ConfigurePwmPeriod(channel, period_us) picks the range, mantissa and exponent, and returns InvalidParameter outside 250 µs to 72.7 ms. ConfigurePwmPeriodRaw() writes the fields directly. Dither ¶ Dither overlays a triangular or trapezoidal wave on the setpoint to reduce a valve's hysteresis (section 4.7): Quantity Formula Amplitude I Dither = STEPS × STEP_SIZE × 2 A / (2 15 − 1) Period T Dither = (4 × STEPS + 2 × FLAT ) × t ref_clk Reference clock t ref_clk = MANT × 2 EXP / f SYS ( DITHER_CLK_DIV ) ConfigureDither(channel, amplitude_mA, frequency_Hz) uses 16 steps and 2 flat steps, derives t ref_clk from the frequency and STEP_SIZE from the amplitude, and enables setpoint synchronisation so a new averaging window starts with each setpoint write. Keep I set − I Dither above zero and I set + I Dither inside the measurement range. Dither stops while the setpoint is 0. No dither clock, no feedback DITHER_CLK_DIV resets to 0. With t ref_clk = 0 the measurement period is 0 and the averaged feedback ( FB_DC , FB_I_AVG , FB_VBAT ) never updates. Call ConfigureDither() (any amplitude, including 0) or ConfigureDitherClock() for every channel whose current you read. Current feedback ¶ Each channel measures its current over T meas and publishes mantissa / exponent results (section 4.10.2). The average current is I avg = 4 A × I_AVG_MANT / TP_MANT with I_AVG_MANT signed (from FB_I_AVG ) and TP_MANT the measurement window (from FB_DC ). A small TP_MANT means no window has completed, so the driver refuses to divide by it: Call Use it for Blocks When there is no window GetAverageCurrent(ch) Console, diagnostics Up to about 8 ms (freezes, polls FB_UPD ) FeedbackNotReady GetDutyCycle(ch) Duty in permyriad (0 to 10000) No Returns 0 ReadChannelFeedback(ch) Average, min / max current and period, VBAT, in one freeze Up to the timeout (10 ms default) TimeoutError SampleChannelCurrents(mask) Control loops: several channels, one burst Never The channel's bit is clear in valid_mask SampleChannelCurrents() returns a CurrentFeedbackBatch : per-channel iavg_ma , the measurement window, and rejected_chains , which counts read chains discarded because replies arrived out of order. Parallel channels ¶ Channels CH0/CH3, CH1/CH2 and CH4/CH5 can drive one load together (section 4.5.2): ParallelPair Master Slave CH0_CH3 CH0 CH3 CH1_CH2 CH1 CH2 CH4_CH5 CH4 CH5 Enable the pair in Config Mode with SetParallelOperation() , then configure and drive only the master, passing parallel_mode = true to the setpoint and dither calls. The slave's MODE and SETPOINT writes are ignored and read back zero. In parallel mode one TARGET LSB is worth twice the current. // Config Mode only: CH0 and CH3 driven as one 2.7 A output. Only the master (CH0) is configured. bool configure_parallel ( Driver & driver ) { if ( ! driver . SetParallelOperation ( tle92466ed :: ParallelPair :: CH0_CH3 , true )) { return false ; } return driver . SetCurrentSetpoint ( Channel :: CH0 , 2000 , /*parallel_mode=*/ true ). has_value (); } Next: Diagnostics and faults .

docs.text: Diagnostics and faults ¶ The chip's operation states, what it monitors, how faults reach FAULTN and the registers, and how the driver reports them. Section references are to the datasheet (Rev. 1.2). Operation states ¶ stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Reset: power-on or RESN low Reset --> Config: supplies in range, RESN high Config --> Mission: OP_MODE = 1 and no blocking fault Mission --> Config: OP_MODE = 0, supply fault, SPI watchdog, clock too slow, ECC error Config --> CriticalFault: clock too fast, internal supply fault Mission --> CriticalFault: clock too fast, internal supply fault CriticalFault --> Reset: power-on or RESN low State What works Driver Reset SPI answers with 16-bit replies; registers return to their defaults on exit HoldReset() / ReleaseReset() , Init() Config Mode Registers; all channels off; channel mode, global configuration, parallel pairs and the PLL can be changed only here Init() ends here; EnterConfigMode() Mission Mode Channels switch and their diagnostics run EnterMissionMode() , EnterMissionModeChecked() Critical Fault Every SPI reply is a critical-fault frame; FAULTN low Reads fail with FaultDetected ( SPI protocol ) EnterMissionMode() sets OP_MODE in CH_CTRL and trusts it. EnterMissionModeChecked() also polls FB_STAT.INIT_DONE until the chip confirms the transition, or times out. Calls that need a state check it: EnableChannel() returns WrongMode in Config Mode, ConfigureChannel() , SetChannelMode() , ConfigureGlobal() and SetParallelOperation() return WrongMode in Mission Mode. What the chip monitors ¶ Group Faults Effect Where the driver reports it External supplies VBAT, VIO, VDD under- and over-voltage Outputs off; Config Mode except for VBAT DeviceStatus , FaultReport ( vbat_uv , vio_ov , ...) Internal supplies 2V5, reference, bias, pre-regulator, ADC Outputs off, Config Mode or Critical Fault FaultReport ( vdd2v5_uv , ref_ov , hvadc_err , ...) Clock Clock too slow (Config Mode), too fast (Critical Fault), reference missing clock_fault , critical-fault flags Temperature Central and per-channel pre-warning and shutdown Channel off at shutdown ot_warning , ot_error , per channel over_temperature Memory Register ECC, OTP ECC, OTP not programmed REG_ECC_ERR forces Config Mode reg_ecc_err , otp_ecc_err , otp_virgin SPI Watchdog expired Config Mode spi_wd_error Per channel, on Open load or short to ground (OLSG), over-current Channel off on over-current FaultReport::channels[n] Per channel, off Open load (OL) and short to ground (SG), with the diagnosis current sources open_load , short_to_ground Per channel, control Current regulation and PWM regulation warnings current_regulation_warning , pwm_regulation_warning Init() refuses a part whose OTP is not programmed ( OTP_VIRGIN , ConfigurationError ): its current calibration would be invalid. It clears a latched REG_ECC_ERR and continues if the bit comes back. Channel diagnosis ¶ Diagnosis runs only in Mission Mode (section 4.9): On-state (channel enabled, setpoint above 0): the current through the shunt is checked. An open load and a short to ground look the same here and are reported together as OLSG. Over-current switches the channel off; the threshold is 2.05 A to 6 A. Off-state (channel enabled with setpoint 0, or setpoint set and channel disabled, with EN high): internal high- and low-side current sources test the LOAD pin voltage and tell OL from SG. ChannelConfig::diag_current sets the source current; SetOffStateDiagnostics() enables the off-state over-current check and the fixed open-load threshold. Use both: the on-state check finds that something is wrong, the off-state check says what. FAULTN ¶ FAULTN goes low in the Critical Fault state, while RESN is low, and on any fault that is not masked in FAULT_MASK0..2 . IsFault() reads the pin (through your port's GpioRead() ); IsFault(true) also prints the full report. Mask a source with SetFaultMask() (Config Mode), or keep a channel out of FAULTN with SetFaultContributionMask() . Reading and clearing faults ¶ void handle_faults ( Driver & driver ) { auto pin = driver . IsFault (); // FAULTN low? if ( ! pin || !* pin ) { return ; } auto report = driver . GetAllFaults (); if ( ! report ) { return ; } if ( report -> vbat_uv || report -> vdd_uv ) { std :: printf ( "supply under-voltage \n " ); } for ( unsigned n = 0 ; n < report -> channels . size (); ++ n ) { const auto & c = report -> channels [ n ]; if ( c . open_load || c . short_to_ground || c . overcurrent || c . over_temperature ) { std :: printf ( "CH%u: OL=%d SG=%d OC=%d OT=%d \n " , n , c . open_load , c . short_to_ground , c . overcurrent , c . over_temperature ); } } ( void ) driver . ClearFaults (); // after the cause is fixed; a fault that is still there comes back } GetAllFaults() reads GLOBAL_DIAG0..2 , FB_STAT and the channel diagnosis registers into one FaultReport ; GetDeviceStatus() and GetChannelDiagnostics() give smaller views. The diagnosis bits are write-1-to-clear: ClearFaults() writes ones to every diagnosis register. A bit that is set again at once means the cause is still there. SPI watchdog ¶ With GlobalConfig::spi_watchdog_enabled , the chip counts WD_TIME in WD_RELOAD down at f SPI,WD = f SYS / 2 14 (about 1.71 kHz, 0.585 ms per count). When it reaches 0, SPI_WD_ERR is set and the chip drops to Config Mode, switching every channel off. WD_TIME Timeout 100 about 58 ms 1000 about 585 ms 10000 about 5.9 s // With GlobalConfig::spi_watchdog_enabled, call this faster than the watchdog runs out. bool kick_watchdog ( Driver & driver ) { return driver . ReloadSpiWatchdog ( 1000 ). has_value (); } Reload it from the task that owns the driver, faster than the timeout. Init() leaves the watchdog off. docs.text: Hardware ¶ What to connect between your MCU and a TLE92466ED, with which bus settings and supplies, and the board-level details that decide whether the first frame works. All values here come from the TLE92466ED datasheet (Rev. 1.2, 2022-02-01). When they disagree with a board's schematic, the schematic wins for pin routing and active levels. Host interface pins ¶ Signal (pin) Direction Notes CSN (5) in Active low; internal pull-up SCK (6) in Internal pull-down SI (7) in MOSI; internal pull-down SO (9) out MISO, push-pull at VIO; tri-state while CSN is high VIO (8) supply The MCU's I/O rail, 3.3 V or 5 V The SPI inputs accept 3.3 V or 5 V logic (V IH 2 V maximum, V IL 0.8 V minimum); the pull-up and pull-downs are 10 µA to 50 µA. SO tri-states within 200 ns after CSN rises, so the chip can share a bus with other devices. Control pins ¶ The driver addresses RESN, EN and FAULTN by name ( tle92466ed::CtrlPin ) and by state ( GpioSignal::ACTIVE / INACTIVE ). Your port maps a state to a level, so the same driver code works with inverted or level-shifted signals. Pin (number) Direction What it does Driver use RESN (26) in, active low Resets every register, all channels off Pulsed by Init() ; HoldReset() , ReleaseReset() EN (27) in, active high Enables the outputs; SPI works when low Set by Init() ; Enable() , Disable() FAULTN (11) open drain, active low Signals a fault; usable as an interrupt IsFault() ; pull it up to VIO DRV0, DRV1 (25, 28) in Drive channels in DIRECT_DRIVE_DRV0/1 Not driven by the driver CLK (24) in External PLL clock, 1 MHz to 8 MHz ConfigureClockSource() FAULTN sinks 2 mA at 0.4 V maximum; leave it open if you do not use it. The PLL runs from the internal oscillator or, with EXT_CLK set in CLK_DIV , from CLK; f SYS is 28 MHz either way (27.5 MHz to 28.5 MHz). Power stage pins ¶ Channel LOADx FWDx GNDPx CH0 1 2 3 CH1 18 17 16 CH2 19 20 21 CH3 36 35 34 CH4 31 32 33 CH5 13 14 15 GND is pins 4, 10, 12, 23 and 30, and the exposed cooling tab. Connect every GNDPx to GND externally and the tab to GND and the heat-sink copper. Load connection ¶ Each channel is a low-side switch: connect the load between its supply and LOADx. The current flows through the internal shunt and the DMOS to GNDPx while the channel is on. Inductive loads need the freewheeling diode at FWDx The chip has no internal freewheeling diode. For a solenoid or valve, fit a diode from FWDx (anode) to the load supply (cathode), as the datasheet's application diagram (section 6) shows. Without it the coil current has no path when the switch opens, and the measured average current is wrong. The datasheet recommends 4.7 nF to 10 nF ceramic capacitors at the load connector and at FWDx. Channels CH0/CH3, CH1/CH2 and CH4/CH5 can be wired in parallel for one load: connect both LOAD pins to the load and both FWD pins to the diode, and configure the pair as described in Current control . Bus settings ¶ Setting Value Mode SPI mode 1 (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 1): SI sampled on the falling SCK edge, SO shifted on the rising edge Bit order MSB first, both directions Frame Exactly 32 bits per CSN low period; any other length is ignored Speed Up to 8 MHz (f SCK ); the examples run at 1 MHz Integrity CRC-8 SAE J1850 in bits [31:24] of every frame ( SPI protocol ) Reply Clocked out during the next frame Watchdog Optional SPI watchdog: reload WD_RELOAD before it reaches 0 ( Diagnostics ) Timing ¶ Parameter Limit Meaning SCK high, low (t SCKH , t SCKL ) ≥ 50 ns 8 MHz maximum clock Enable lead (t CSN_LEAD ) ≥ 250 ns CSN falling to the first SCK rising edge Enable lag (t CSN_LAG ) ≥ 250 ns Last SCK falling edge to CSN rising Transfer delay (t CSN_TD ) ≥ 600 ns CSN high time between two frames SI setup, hold (t SI_SU , t SI_H ) ≥ 20 ns Around the falling SCK edge SO valid (t SO_V ) ≤ 100 ns 150 pF load SO enable, disable (t SO_EN , t SO_DIS ) ≤ 200 ns From CSN falling, rising Reset to logic ready (t RESN ) ≤ 0.1 ms After RESN goes high Power-on reset (t POR ) ≤ 10 ms After the supplies are in range The transfer delay matters on fast SPI peripherals: two frames sent back to back need CSN high for at least 600 ns between them. docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake or ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 12+ or a current MSVC. On C++23 the driver uses std::expected ; on C++20 it uses the polyfill in inc/tle92466ed_expected.hpp . A little-endian target: the frame CRC is computed over the frame's bytes in memory, and a static_assert stops the build on a big-endian one. No RTOS, heap or exceptions: every call is noexcept and returns a tle92466ed::DriverResult<T> . docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the SPI interface. The driver never calls your SDK directly. It calls twelve methods on a class you derive from tle92466ed::SpiInterface<Self> (in inc/tle92466ed_spi_interface.hpp ). The base class uses CRTP: the calls are resolved at compile time, so there are no virtual functions, no vtable and nothing to allocate. Frame building, the CRC, the pipeline and reply validation are in the base class; your port only moves words and toggles pins. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one Driver object per chip. The core owns the chip's register map (from inc/tle92466ed_registers.hpp): the central configuration and status registers, and the bank of channel registers that repeats for each of the six channels. The communication interface (tle92466ed::SpiInterface in inc/tle92466ed_spi_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base: it builds 32-bit frames with the CRC-8 SAE J1850 byte, runs the one-frame reply pipeline and validates every reply; the methods it dispatches to your class are listed from the header. The platform port is the only code you write. Below it is the chip. What you implement ¶ Method Contract Init() Bring up the SPI peripheral and the GPIOs. Called first, from Driver::Init() Deinit() Release them Transfer32(tx) One full-duplex 32-bit frame, MSB first, CSN low for exactly 32 clocks. Return the received word TransferMulti(tx, rx) tx.size() frames in order, one CSN pulse each, without another device's traffic in between GpioSet(pin, signal) Drive RESN or EN to ACTIVE / INACTIVE GpioRead(pin) Read FAULTN as ACTIVE (low) / INACTIVE Delay(us) Block for at least that many microseconds (the driver waits up to 50 ms at a time) Configure(config) Apply an SPIConfig (frequency, mode) if your port supports changing it; otherwise succeed IsReady() true after a successful Init() GetLastError() , ClearErrors() Your port's sticky error, if it keeps one Log(level, tag, fmt, va_list) Print one line; Error ... Verbose . Add using SpiInterface<Self>::Log; Each returns a tle92466ed::CommResult<T> ; return tle::unexpected(CommError::...) on failure. The C++20 concept SpiInterfaceLike checks the core signatures at compile time. Keep the base Log() visible The driver calls the base class's printf-style Log(level, tag, fmt, ...) . The driver calls this first, from Init(). Result < void > Init () noexcept { ready_ = platform_spi_init (); return ready_ ? Result < void > {} : tle :: unexpected ( Error :: HardwareNotReady ); } Result < void > Deinit () noexcept { ready_ = false ; return {}; } // One 32-bit frame, MSB first, CSN low for exactly these four bytes. Start at 1 MHz. Exactly 32 bits per CSN low period. The chip ignores a frame of any other length. A 4-byte transfer is fine; a 3- or 5-byte one is not. A CSN pulse per frame in TransferMulti() , with CSN high for at least 600 ns between frames (t CSN_TD ). Most SPI drivers that toggle CS per transaction meet this at 1 MHz; check it at 8 MHz. No other device between the frames of one call. The reply to the command frame comes out during the next frame; if another device's transaction runs in between, the reply is lost. On a shared bus take the bus lock for the whole TransferMulti() call ( spi_device_acquire_bus() on ESP-IDF, a mutex elsewhere). Bit 31 first. Transfer32() takes and returns the frame as a uint32_t ; put bit 31 on the wire first. On a little-endian MCU with a byte-buffer SPI API that means swapping the bytes, as the port above does. Return an error only for a bus failure. CRC, status and reply-width problems are the base class's job. Control-pin levels ¶ Pin ACTIVE level on the chip Port mapping on a direct connection RESN Low (reset) ACTIVE writes 0 EN High (outputs enabled) ACTIVE writes 1 FAULTN Low (fault) Pin reads 0: return ACTIVE Invert the mapping in your port when a buffer or level shifter inverts a signal; the driver code stays the same. FAULTN is open drain: enable a pull-up on the MCU or fit one to VIO. Reference implementation ¶ The ESP32 examples use esp32_tle92466ed_bus.hpp : an ESP-IDF spi_master port with one spi_device_transmit() per frame, GPIO control for RESN and EN, and ESP_LOG output. It assumes the TLE92466ED has the bus to itself: it does not take the bus lock across TransferMulti() . Start from it for any ESP-IDF target and add spi_device_acquire_bus() if the bus is shared. Check your port ¶ Build it: the port on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over it. Call Init() . DeviceNotResponding means MISO stayed idle. WrongDeviceID with an ICVID such as 0x82xx or 0x60xx ( 0xC1 shifted by one bit) means the sampling edge is wrong: check the SPI mode. Read ReadAllSupplyVoltages() : a plausible VBAT and VDD prove 22-bit feedback reads end to end. Enable the SPI watchdog with a short WD_TIME and stop reloading it: SPI_WD_ERR must appear in GetAllFaults() , which proves writes land. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each TLE92466ED one owner task, or guard every call on a driver object (and its port) with one mutex. Several chips on separate ports can run in parallel. Next: Examples .

docs.text: SPI protocol ¶ The TLE92466ED's 32-bit frames, the CRC, the one-frame reply pipeline, and what the driver does to make every access trustworthy. The frame definitions are in section 5.2.3 of the datasheet ; the driver's types are tle92466ed::SPIFrame , ReplyMode , SPIStatus and CriticalFaultFlags in inc/tle92466ed_spi_interface.hpp . Frames ¶ Every frame is 32 bits, MSB first, inside one CSN low period. A frame of any other length is ignored. The host sends one of two request frames: Bits Write frame (R/W = 1) Read frame (R/W = 0) 31:24 CRC CRC 23:17 ADDRESS , 7 bits don't care (the driver sends 0) 16 R/W = 1 R/W = 0 15:0 DATA ADDRESS , 16 bits The asymmetry matters: a write can address only 0x00 to 0x7F , which holds every writable register (the central configuration and the six channel banks). The status and feedback registers at 0x200 and above are read-only by construction. The chip answers with one of three reply frames, chosen by the register that was read: Bits 16-bit reply ( REPLY_16BIT , 00B) 22-bit reply ( REPLY_22BIT , 01B) Critical fault ( CRITICAL_FAULT , 10B) 31:24 CRC CRC don't care 23:22 00 01 10 21:17 STATUS DATA[21:17] don't care 16 R/W of the previous request DATA[16] don't care 15:8 DATA[15:8] DATA[15:8] don't care 7:0 DATA[7:0] DATA[7:0] 1V5 2V5 BG CLK_TOO_SLOW CLK_TOO_FAST DIG_CLK_TOO_SLOW DIG_CLK_TOO_FAST WD_REF_CLK Feedback registers ( FB_STAT , FB_VOLTAGE1/2 and the channel feedback bank at +0x200 ) answer with 22-bit replies; every other register with 16-bit replies. Status field ¶ The status in a 16-bit reply describes the previous request frame: STATUS SPIStatus Meaning 00000 NO_ERROR Accepted 00001 SPI_FRAME_ERROR Malformed 00010 CRC_ERROR CRC mismatch 00011 WRITE_RO_REG Wrote a read-only register 00100 - 00110 INTERNAL_BUS_FAULT Internal bus fault The lowest code has the highest priority. Write() turns any non-zero status into CommError::TransferError ( DriverError::SPIFrameError ). CRC ¶ Every frame carries a CRC-8 SAE J1850 byte in bits [31:24] : Parameter Value Polynomial x 8 + x 4 + x 3 + x 2 + 1 ( 0x1D ) Initial value 0xFF Final XOR 0xFF Input order frame [7:0] , then [15:8] , then [23:16] (the reverse of the wire order) Check value 0x4B for the ASCII string 123456789 CalculateCrc8J1850() and CalculateFrameCrc() implement it; the host tests check the standard check value and the byte order. The chip checks incoming CRCs only while CRC_EN in GLOBAL_CONFIG is set. The driver always sends a correct CRC, clears CRC_EN in Init() and sets it again when you pass GlobalConfig::crc_enabled = true to ConfigureGlobal() . Reply CRCs are checked on every read whatever CRC_EN says. The reply pipeline ¶ The reply to a frame comes out of SO during the next frame. A read therefore needs a second frame to collect its answer, and that answer depends on what the bus did before. The driver makes each access independent of history by sending three frames: Frame MOSI MISO carries 1, flush read 0x0000 The reply still pending from earlier traffic: discarded 2, command the read or write The reply to frame 1: discarded 3, dummy read 0x0000 The reply to frame 2: kept The dummies read address 0 rather than repeating the command: on the bench a repeated read made the part answer with a reserved reply mode. ReadMulti() uses the same idea for a burst: flush, N commands, dummy, N + 2 frames for N reads. How a reply is validated ¶ A reply is accepted only when all of these hold: MISO was driven (the word is not 0x00000000 or 0xFFFFFFFF ), otherwise CommError::NoReply . The CRC matches. The reply mode is the width the register is defined to answer with ( ExpectedReplyFor() ), so a stale 16-bit reply cannot pass as a 22-bit feedback value. Read() makes two attempts before it gives up with CRCError (frames arrived, none were well formed) or NoReply . A critical-fault reply is not retried: it means the chip cannot serve any access, and the read fails with CommError::BusError ( DriverError::FaultDetected ). LastCriticalFaultFlags() and SawCriticalFault() keep the fault byte for the caller. Fault frames and the CRC check The datasheet marks bits [31:24] of a critical-fault frame as don't care, but Read() checks the CRC before it looks at the reply mode. A fault frame whose top byte does not happen to match the CRC is therefore reported as CRCError , not FaultDetected . When reads fail with CRCError right after power-up, check the supplies as well as the bus. Critical fault frames ¶ The chip answers every access with a critical-fault frame while it is in the Critical Fault state: an internal supply (1V5, 2V5, ADC bandgap) or the clock is out of range. Bits 7 to 5 are "OK" flags (1 = good); bits 4 to 0 are fault flags (1 = fault). Bit Flag 1 means 7 1V5 1.5 V internal supply OK 6 2V5 2.5 V internal supply OK 5 BG ADC bandgap OK 4 CLK_TOO_SLOW Clock too slow for operation 3 CLK_TOO_FAST Clock too fast for operation 2 DIG_CLK_TOO_SLOW Digital clock too slow (clock watchdog enabled) 1 DIG_CLK_TOO_FAST Digital clock too fast (clock watchdog enabled) 0 WD_REF_CLK Clock watchdog reference clock missing A fault byte of 0x00 (all three supplies "not OK") almost always means VDD is missing, not an SPI problem. Chip select and shared buses ¶ The datasheet ends every access with a rising CSN edge, so each 32-bit frame needs its own CSN pulse, with at least 600 ns of CSN high between frames. What must not happen between the frames of one access is another device's transaction: the reply of the TLE92466ED's command would be clocked out during someone else's frame and lost. On a shared bus, hold the bus (a mutex, spi_device_acquire_bus() on ESP-IDF) for the whole TransferMulti() call. Porting has the rules for the port. Next: Current control .

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms you may see while bringing up a TLE92466ED, their causes and the fix for each, cheapest check first. Start with the error a call returns and, once Init() has passed, with GetAllFaults() : the error tells bus problems (no reply, bad replies) apart from chip state (wrong mode, a fault the chip reports). Bring-up ¶ Symptom Cause Fix Init() returns DeviceNotResponding MISO idle: no VIO, CSN not reaching the chip, MISO not connected Measure VIO at pin 8; scope CSN and SO during Init() Init() returns FaultDetected Every reply is a critical-fault frame VDD (4.5 V to 5.5 V at pin 29) first, then the clock source Reads fail with CRCError right after power-up A critical-fault frame whose top byte is not a valid CRC ( SPI protocol ) Check VDD as for FaultDetected Init() returns WrongDeviceID ICVID is not 0xC1xx : bits shifted by a wrong SPI mode, or another device on the same CSN SPI mode 1; one CSN per device Init() returns ConfigurationError OTP_VIRGIN : the part's calibration OTP is not programmed Use a production part CRCError or SPIFrameError now and then Frames not exactly 32 bits, CSN high time under 600 ns, clock too fast for the wiring One 4-byte transfer per CSN; lower SCK to 1 MHz; shorten the wires Wrong values on a shared bus Another device's frame between the command and its reply Hold the bus lock for the whole TransferMulti() ( Porting ) Channels ¶ Symptom Cause Fix EnableChannel() returns WrongMode Still in Config Mode EnterMissionMode() first ConfigureChannel() or SetChannelMode() returns WrongMode In Mission Mode EnterConfigMode() , configure, then go back Channel enabled, no current EN low (all channels off), setpoint 0, or the chip dropped to Config Mode Enable() ; IsMissionMode() ; GetAllFaults() for supply or watchdog faults Channel drops out after a while SPI watchdog expired: the chip returns to Config Mode Reload it faster ( Diagnostics ) or leave it off Current far from the setpoint No freewheeling diode at FWDx, setpoint above the specified 1.5 A, parallel_mode missing on a pair Hardware , Current control SetCurrentSetpoint() returns InvalidParameter Above 2000 mA (4000 mA in parallel) Lower it; pass parallel_mode = true for a pair A parallel pair drives half the current The slave was configured instead of the master Configure and drive CH0, CH1 or CH4 only Feedback ¶ Symptom Cause Fix GetAverageCurrent() returns FeedbackNotReady DITHER_CLK_DIV still 0, so the measurement period is 0 ConfigureDither() or ConfigureDitherClock() on that channel Feedback frozen at an old value FB_FRZ left set by an interrupted snapshot ReleaseFeedbackFreeze() SampleChannelCurrents() sets rejected_chains Replies arrived out of order on the bus Bus integrity: shared-bus lock, wiring, SCK speed ReadChannelFeedback() returns TimeoutError No feedback update within the timeout Longer timeout, or a faster dither (shorter measurement period) Faults ¶ Symptom Cause Fix FAULTN low before Init() RESN low, or latched power-on flags Init() releases RESN and clears the power-on flags; then read GetAllFaults() A fault returns right after ClearFaults() The cause is still there Read GetAllFaults() ; the flag names the cause open_load on a fitted coil Open-load threshold too high for the current, or the load is wired to the wrong LOAD pin Lower open_load_threshold ;
